items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between calls; the program resends the message history each call. Option a or d shows the belief that the model or window remembers by itself; c confuses memory with training.

Call 1 receives 1,000 tokens, call 2 receives 1,000 + 500 = 1,500, and call 3 receives 1,000 + 1,000 = 2,000, because each call resends everything so far. Total 4,500. An answer of 2,000 counts only the final context; 2,000 + 500 style sums miss the resending.

An exact fact with one correct value, needed across sessions, belongs in a persistent database the program looks up. Message history is gone after the session, the model does not learn, and putting every student in the prompt does not scale.

items.answer: It would cost far too much and exceed or degrade the context; only a few relevant chunks are needed.
accepted: it would exceed the context window
it would be too costly because every call resends it
items.rationale: Every call resends the context and is billed per token; 600,000 tokens would also not fit or would hurt the model's recall (context rot). Any of cost, window limit or reduced accuracy is a full answer.
The model sees only what retrieval returned. A missed chunk means the model cannot use it and may answer from guesswork; retrieval quality must be tested separately from answer quality.
